newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil stocks low after selling frenzy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil stocks low after selling frenzy.

text.p: Unusually high prices for oil products have sunk Singapore stocks to their lowest level in at least three years after a selling frenzy, traders said on Friday.
But a huge wave of imports is heading towards Singapore, which could see stocks replenished as soon as next week, they said.
"In such a deeply backwardated market it does not make sense to hold on to the oil," one trader at an oil major said.
In such a market, spot oil prices are than for oil sold for delivery at a later date.

The market took such a shape because of a buying spree by local trader firm Hin Leong Trading, which spent more than U.S.$220 million in March on more than seven million barrels of diesel and 1.4 million barrels of jet fuel, traders said.

As a result, stocks in Singapore for key industrial oil products such as diesel and fuel oil plummetted to their lowest level since at least January 1994, figures released by the Trade Development Board (TDB) on Thursday showed.

The TDB data showed residual fuel oil stocks for the week ending April 2 fell by 2.435 million barrels to 8.229 million barrels. Stocks of diesel and kerosene plunged 1.175 million barrels to 4.953 million barrels.
"The figures show that the refineries here are dry," another trader said.
Traders said sellers were offloading as many cargoes for promt delivery locking in hefty premiums by hedging their positions in the swaps market.

Apart from the high premiums for prompt delivery, low stocks were also due partly to the shutdown of the 280,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Mobil refinery since March 16 for a six-week maintenance, traders said.
In addition, Singapore Refining Co only restarted a 90,000-bpd crude unit on March 23 after a scheduled 19-day closure and would only now build its inventories.

Traders said the impact of Hin Leong's large purchases were being seen through the stock figures as it has taken delivery of around 1.76 million barrels of diesel and about 900,000-barrels of jet-kerosene over the last 10 days, they said.
Hin Leong's purchases have triggered the largest West-to-East flow of diesel in years and at the same time given refiners their best returns in more than a year.

The low stocks of most oil traders and some refiners will only be replenished some time next week when the first of the estimated 1.0-1.6 million tonnes of diesel start to arrive from the West, where prices are lower.

Hin Leong does not maintain a huge storage space in Singapore as sister company Ocean Tankers has a large tanker fleet, including five very large crude carriers (VLCC), which it can use as offshore storage. A VLCC carries 160,000 to 320,000 tonnes of cargo.
Oil products stored in such a fashion outside Singapore's territorial waters are not included in the Singapore stock information.
